messages:
Maya: Heads up 1: Horizon observed a short-lived isolation for a Dedicated customer after peering maintenance at ~02:40 UTC. Opening thread for postmortem follow-ups.
Gabe: Thanks. Symptoms?
Maya: TCP resets, odd SYN retransmits, some services timed out for ~7m. Customer reported failed healthchecks to on-prem DB.
Rina: From our side trace: burst of ICMP fragmentation followed by route withdrawals to the peer set. Could be packet size + BGP instability combo.
Lia (oncall): Collected pcap and SYSLOG from edge during event window. Uploading to incident bucket.
ops-bot: Upload complete: s3://incidents/horizon/2280012345/pcap.tgz (sha256: a3f4...).
Gabe: OK assign owners: Rina -> root-cause writeup + MTU sweep, Lia -> customer log confirmation & on-prem changes, Maya -> remediation tracker & rollout plan. Due dates next week unless critical.
Rina: Plan: run MTU probe matrix from all AZs and the customer edge. Script: ```for sz in 1500 1472 1440 1400; do ping -M do -s $sz 10.0.0.1; done``` Will also check if any NAT device is rewriting MSS.
Lia (oncall): Asked customer to run equivalent probes and provide router config snippets. They said they swapped an edge appliance earlier that day.
Maya: Add to remediation tracker with a unique ID. I'll create ticket REM-2280012345 and link to weekly trends dashboard.
ops-bot: New ticket created: REM-2280012345. Link: https://tracker.redwood/REM-2280012345
Gabe: Short-term mitigation: enable MSS clamp on the peering gateway to 1380 as a canary, limit to 1/3 of traffic, monitor for 2 hours. If OK, expand.
Rina: I'll stage the MSS clamp on staging peering and run synthetic load. If staging replicates, schedule canary to prod.
Lia (oncall): Customer willing to schedule brief maintenance tomorrow 00:00-00:30 PDT for their edge appliance if we need config change.
Maya: Postmortem follow-ups (owners + hard due dates):
- Rina: run cross-AZ MTU sweep, verify NAT/MSS rewrite, produce RCA draft (owner: Rina, due: 2280090000).
- Lia: confirm customer edge model+firmware and share config snippet; coordinate maintenance window (owner: Lia, due: 2280055000).
- Gabe: implement fragmentation alert rule and a weekly trending report for peerings showing fragmentation spikes >3% (owner: Gabe, due: 2280040000).
- Maya: create REM ticket, link runbook, and schedule follow-up review in weekly incidents meeting (owner: Maya, due: 2280035000).
All: add ack when you have task accepted.
Rina: Ack. Starting sweep now and will post results.
Lia (oncall): Ack 1. Will check customer edge firmware and post config.
Gabe: Acked. I'll author the alert and add a dashboard card (peering -> fragmentation trends).
ops-bot: Staging deployment report: MSS clamp at 1380 reduced fragmentation to 0.6% under synthetic load. No regressions observed in 30m test.
Maya: Good. Proceed with canary to 34% of production traffic on peering-gw-02 and monitor tcp_retransmits and 5xx rates.
Rina: Canary started. Monitoring window: 60m. If fragmentation stays <1%, plan for full rollout.
Lia (oncall): Customer confirmed their swapped appliance had default MTU 1500 while our peering uses 1420 due to overlay encapsulation. They will patch firmware tomorrow.
Gabe: Update action item: add a checklist to onboarding docs for Dedicated customers about MTU expectations when swapping edge appliances. (owner: Gabe, due: 2280150000).
Maya: Closing criteria: RCA written, REM ticket with owners and dates, alert + dashboard live, and onboarding doc updated. We'll reconvene in 7 days to check for recurrence.
Rina: RCA draft uploaded to REM ticket. Key finding: edge device defaulted to 1500, overlay encapsulation requires lower MTU -> fragmentation -> session resets. Also noted lack of automated fragmentation alert.
Maya: Thanks. I'll mark initial actions in tracker and schedule the 7-day recurrence review.
ops-bot: REM-2280012345 status updated: owners assigned, due dates set, attachments added.
All: any objections to closing this thread and tracking in REM ticket?
Gabe: No objections. Closing here, will follow in tracker. :white_check_mark:
text_summary: Dedicated customer experienced short isolation after peering maintenance. Root cause: MTU mismatch between customer's new edge appliance and Redwood's overlay peering, causing fragmentation and TCP resets. Actions: MSS clamp canary, MTU sweep, customer firmware/config coordination, alert/dashboard creation, onboarding doc update. Owners assigned with due dates and REM ticket created.
